paper.title: Thompson Sampling for Contextual Bandits with Linear Payoffs

settings.name_in_paper: Stochastic contextual bandit with linear payoffs, contexts chosen by an adaptive adversary
unmapped: N arms per round (n_act); the N-free bound also claimed for infinite arms
regret against the best arm at each round given the contexts (realizable linear model)
settings.definition_quote: There are $N$ arms. At time $t = 1, 2, \ldots $, a context vector $b_i(t) \in {\mathbb R}^d$, is revealed for every arm $i$. These context vectors are chosen by an adversary in an adaptive manner after observing the arms played and their rewards up to time $t-1$ ... Given $b_i(t)$, the reward for arm $i$ at time $t$ is generated from an (unknown) distribution with mean $b_i(t)^T\mu$ ... We assume that $\eta_{i,t}=r_i(t)-b_i(t)^T\mu$ is conditionally $R$-sub-Gaussian ... We will also assume that $||b_i(t)||\le 1$, $||\mu||\le 1$, and $\Delta_i(t) \le 1$

algorithms.name: Thompson Sampling for Contextual bandits (Gaussian prior)

extra_assumptions: delta is an input parameter of the algorithm
R treated as constant inside O

source.label: th:dep
source.quote: With probability $1-\delta$, the total regret for Thompson Sampling algorithm in time $T$ is bounded as ${\cal R}(T) = O\left(d^{3/2}\sqrt{T} \left( \ln (T) + \sqrt{\ln(T) \ln(\frac{1}{\delta})}\right)\right)$, or, ${\cal R}(T) = O\left(d\sqrt{T \log(N)} \left( \ln (T) + \sqrt{\ln(T) \ln(\frac{1}{\delta})}\right)\right)$, whichever is smaller, for any $0<\delta<1$, where $\delta$ is a parameter used by the algorithm.

results.notes: Regret is sum of Delta_{a(t)}(t) (pseudo-regret w.r.t. per-round best arm) with high probability. Analyzed version uses v_t depending on t, so anytime. Bound independent of N; remark says applies to infinite arms.
